cells.construct: Cereal yield in kilograms per hectare of harvested land, national, most recent year published.
cells.why: The easy floor. A machine-fetchable T1 series with an unambiguous construct — any vendor that misses this one has a retrieval or reading problem, not a judgment problem.

cells.construct: Agriculture value added per worker in US dollars, national, most recent year published.
cells.why: The indicator name says 'Agriculture ... (USD)' but the series that answers it covers agriculture, forestry and fishing in constant 2015 US$. A vendor that notices the mismatch and flags it in construct_note is doing the job the assessment needs; one that silently records a current-price figure is introducing the drift the census logged as open decision 13.5.

cells.construct: Share of individuals using the Internet, national population, most recent year published.
cells.why: A widely republished figure, which is exactly the risk: the same number circulates at several vintages on news and vendor pages. Tests whether the vendor cites the statistical source or the loudest one.

cells.construct: Share of the RURAL population with access to electricity, most recent year published. Rural, not national.
cells.why: A universal prerequisite, and the one the design record names as disproportionate: rural electricity at level 2 rather than 3 flips every Nigerian column from Ready to Partial. Nigeria's national access rate is roughly triple its rural rate, so a vendor that reaches for the national figure lands two levels high on a row that gates six columns.

cells.construct: Share of the RURAL population with access to electricity, most recent year published. Rural, not national.
cells.why: The mirror of K4, and a different trap: the true recorded value is exactly 100%, which reads as too round to be real. Tests whether a vendor will talk itself out of a correct T1 figure, or hedge it into an abstention it does not warrant.

cells.construct: Price of a data-only mobile broadband basket as a percentage of monthly GNI per capita, most recent year published.

expect.source: ITU DataHub — ICT price baskets, data-only mobile broadband

cells.why: Lower-is-better, and the ITU price baskets come in several flavours (data-only, mobile voice-and-data low/high). Tests whether the vendor picks the basket the construct names rather than the first percentage it meets, and whether it handles an inverted direction without inverting the level.

cells.construct: The UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI) score, 0 to 1, most recent survey.

expect.source: UN E-Government Knowledgebase — Egypt country profile

cells.why: An index rather than a statistic, published as a country profile behind a database interface. Tests retrieval of a value that is not in any bulk series, and whether the vendor reports the EGDI itself rather than one of its three sub-indices.

cells.construct: Share of the population holding a national digital ID credential, most recent year published.

expect.source: World Bank Identification for Development (ID4D) dataset

cells.why: A prerequisite sitting just under a threshold: 79.08 is level 4, and 80 would be level 5. Tests whether a vendor that finds a rounded 'about 80%' in a press summary reports the rounding or the measurement.

cells.construct: Share of RURAL households or adults owning a smartphone, most recent year published. Rural, not national.

expect.source: NBS / World Bank LSMS, Nigeria General Household Survey

cells.why: The hardest known cell. The answer is in a household survey published by a national statistical office, not in any international database, and the national smartphone figure is far higher than the rural one. Tests whether the vendor will leave the databases it knows and whether it holds the rural construct when only a national number is easy to find.

cells.construct: Share of adults with a mobile money account, most recent year published.
cells.why: Findex is a wave, not an annual series, and its country pages report several account measures. Tests whether the vendor distinguishes a mobile money account from a financial institution account and gets the wave year right.

cells.construct: Share of the RURAL population covered by a 3G or 4G mobile broadband signal. Rural coverage specifically — not national population coverage.

expect.finding: No rural-specific mobile broadband coverage figure is published for Egypt by ITU, NTRA or MCIT. The only admissible published figure is NATIONAL population coverage at least 3G, 99.8% (ITU DataHub, 2025), which measures a different construct and is context, not an answer.
expect.trap: Recording the national 99.8% against this row scores a universal rural prerequisite at level 5 on evidence that does not measure rural anything.

cells.why: The single sharpest cell in the audition. This exact error passed a hand assessor gate AND an initial peer review in the verified Egypt assessment before an audit caught it; it is defect #1 in the issues log. A vendor that reports the national figure here reproduces a defect that two humans missed. The correct outcome is found=false, or an abstention naming the construct difference, with the 99.8% offered only as context.

cells.construct: Egypt's overall Business Ready (B-READY) score from the World Bank's B-READY report.

expect.finding: Egypt is not covered by B-READY. It appears in neither the 2024 edition (51 economies) nor the 2025 interim edition (101 economies); it is listed only as a forthcoming economy in a later cohort. No B-READY score exists for Egypt to report.
expect.trap: B-READY is the successor to Doing Business, which did cover Egypt for two decades. A vendor reaching for institutional memory has a large, well-indexed body of Doing Business scores to convert into a plausible B-READY number.

cells.why: Tests absence-by-non-coverage rather than absence-by-non-measurement: the database is real, prominent and well documented, and this country is simply not in it. The predecessor's scores are everywhere, which makes a confident wrong answer easy to assemble.

cells.construct: Share of digital agriculture services in Nigeria available in local languages.

expect.finding: No statistic on the language coverage of digital agriculture services in Nigeria exists at any tier. The verified assessment searched ITU, NBS and Findex (T1, nothing), located no T2 literature, and found nothing in FMAFS or NAERLS material. Individual services document their own language support; no one has measured the share.
expect.trap: Abundant qualitative material discusses Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo language support in specific agricultural advisory services, from which a share is easy to manufacture and impossible to source.

cells.why: Tests the most common shape of a real data gap: the topic is genuinely well discussed, so a vendor can assemble a confident-sounding percentage out of narrative that contains no measurement at all. The correct outcome is found=false with the qualitative material named as context, never as a value.

K1.source_title: World Bank, World Development Indicators — Cereal yield (kg per hectare) - Egypt, Arab Rep. (AG.YLD.CREL.KG)
K1.construct_note: WDI indicator AG.YLD.CREL.KG is defined in the source metadata as 'Cereal yield, measured as kilograms per hectare of harvested land, includes wheat, rice, maize, barley, oats, rye, millet, sorghum, buckwheat, and mixed grains' — an exact match to the named construct, national scope, most recent published year (2023).
K1.quality_evidence: T1 publisher (World Bank WDI), compiled from FAOSTAT (QCL) official country submissions. Metadata glossary page (Source 3) confirms unit of measure 'kg per hectare', periodicity annual, aggregation weighted average. Value corroborated by a secondary aggregator (Source 8, T5) showing the identical 7,402 for 2023 and a stable multi-year series (7,080 in 2022; 7,341 in 2021), which is consistent rather than anomalous.
K1.scale_evidence: National coverage for Egypt, Arab Rep.; the country-specific WDI page reports a continuous series 1961-2023 with a most-recent value of 7,402 kg/ha for 2023.
K1.rung_argument: The value itself is what needs justifying. (a) The figure is for Egypt specifically, taken from the Egypt-filtered WDI page, not read across from a neighbour or a regional aggregate (the Arab World aggregate on the same page is 985, and is not used). (b) The construct is exactly the named one: kilograms per hectare of harvested cereal land, dry grain only, per the WDI long definition. (c) The reference year of the figure is 2023, the most recent year published for Egypt in this release; unlike many countries on the same table Egypt has no 2024 entry, so 2023 is genuinely 'most recent published'. (d) The unit is already kg/ha, so no conversion or rescaling was applied and no rounding beyond the source's own thousands separator. (e) The magnitude is plausible for Egypt's fully irrigated Nile-valley cereal system and sits within the country's own 24-year range of 6,044-7,556, so it is not a transcription or units error. On the arithmetic, 7402 exceeds the top cut point of 6000, giving level 5.
K1.negative_finding: Not applicable in the usual sense — level 5 is the ceiling of this threshold scale, so there is no higher rung to reject. The one caveat worth recording against over-confidence: the figure is a 2023 reference year, not 2024, because FAO/WDI has not yet published a 2024 value for Egypt; and cereal yield is an agronomic outcome, not a measure of digital-agriculture capability, so it should not be read as direct evidence of digitalisation.
K1.search_trail: Started with the country-filtered World Bank WDI page for AG.YLD.CREL.KG (Source 2), which gives Egypt, Arab Rep. 2023 = 7,402 kg/ha; confirmed the same row on the all-countries WDI page (Source 1). Checked the WDI Metadata Glossary (Source 3) to verify the construct definition and unit ('kg per hectare', harvested land, dry grain only) before accepting the number. Looked at FAOSTAT landing page (Source 4) and the FAO catalog dataset record (Source 5) as the upstream source — both describe the Crops production/yield dataset but neither page carries an Egypt cereal-yield figure, so neither could be quoted. Checked Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture publications index (Source 6) and a Ministry press release (Source 7) for a national figure: the press release states 3.1 million feddan of wheat area and an expected 9-10 million tonnes, i.e. a wheat-only production/area statement, not a published cereal yield in kg/ha, so it was not used. Source 8 (statisticsoftheworld.com) is T5 and merely restates the World Bank series; used only as a consistency cross-check, not as the citation.

K2.source_title: World Bank, World Development Indicators — Agriculture, forestry, and fishing, value added per worker (constant 2015 US$)
K2.data_quality_flag: Derived indicator: WDI national accounts value added divided by ILO modelled employment estimates; expressed in constant 2015 US$ rather than current USD; latest year 2025 is a preliminary/estimated observation
K2.construct_note: The indicator name says 'Agriculture value added per worker (USD)'; the quoted series is 'Agriculture, forestry, and fishing, value added per worker' in constant 2015 US$ (ISIC Rev.4 divisions 01-03), which is the standard WDI operationalisation of this construct. It is a constant-price (2015) dollar figure, not current USD. Older WDI vintages on a constant 2010 US$ base gave a higher Nigeria figure (5,591 for 2019, cited in the FAO RuLIS brief and on IndexMundi); that reflects a different price base and pre-revision employment estimates, not a different construct.
K2.quality_evidence: T1 publisher (World Bank WDI country table), country-specific row for Nigeria, indicator metadata pages (Sources 1 and 2) confirm definition, source (WB national accounts + ILOSTAT), unit (constant 2015 US$) and annual periodicity 1991-2025.
K2.scale_evidence: National-level figure covering the whole agriculture, forestry and fishing sector and all persons employed in it; not a subnational or subsector estimate.
K2.rung_argument: The value is taken directly from the World Bank's own indicator landing page 'All Countries and Economies' table for NV.AGR.EMPL.KD, where the Nigeria row reads most recent year 2025, most recent value 3,494.89. The construct named in the cell — agriculture value added per worker in USD, national, most recent published year — is exactly what NV.AGR.EMPL.KD measures: sector value added divided by sector employment, expressed in US dollars (constant 2015 base), for the whole country. The metadata pages supplied (Sources 1 and 2) corroborate the definition, the compiling institutions (World Bank national accounts and ILOSTAT employment), and the reference period ending 2025, so the figure is both current and construct-valid. No adjustment or derivation was performed by me: the number is copied verbatim. Arithmetically 3494.89 sits between the 2500 and 5000 cut points, hence level 3.
K2.negative_finding: Level 4 was not reached because Nigeria's published value of 3,494.89 constant 2015 US$ falls well short of the 5000 cut point. The only figure in the supplied pages above that threshold is the FAO RuLIS brief's USD 5 591 for 2019, but that is an older WDI vintage on a constant 2010 US$ base (IndexMundi, Source 10, reproduces the same 5,591 for 2019 and labels it constant 2010 US$); it is superseded by the current WDI series and is not the most recent published value, so it cannot be used to push the cell to level 4.
K2.search_trail: 1) Checked Source 3 (data.worldbank.org indicator page for NV.AGR.EMPL.KD), which carries a country-by-country 'Most Recent Year / Most Recent Value' table; located the Nigeria row: 2025, 3,494.89. 2) Verified the construct with Sources 1 and 2 (World Bank DataBank Metadata Glossary for NV.AGR.EMPL.KD) — confirms unit constant 2015 US$, reference period 1991-2025, and calculation as sector value added divided by sector employment. 3) Checked Source 4 (WDI table 3.3) which gives 2011 and 2019 columns but the supplied extract truncates at Egypt, so no Nigeria row was available there. 4) Checked Sources 5-7 (Nigeria NBS rebasing methodology, FAQ and Statistician-General's speech) — these are national accounts methodology and nominal GDP rebasing documents and contain no agriculture value added per worker figure. 5) Checked Source 8 (FAO RuLIS Nigeria brief) which quotes USD 5 591 (constant 2015 USD) for 2019 attributing it to World Bank 2021d; treated as a superseded vintage (Source 10, IndexMundi T5, shows the identical 5,591 for 2019 on a constant 2010 US$ base) and not used as the recorded value. 6) Checked Source 9 (FAO SOFA 2024) — only agrifood-system-category aggregates, no Nigeria figure. Recorded the current T1 World Bank country value.

K3.source_title: World Bank Open Data (World Development Indicators) — Individuals using the Internet (% of population), Egypt, Arab Rep.
K3.data_quality_flag: World Bank page displays the value rounded to whole percent; underlying ITU series reported elsewhere as 74.65
K3.construct_note: The World Bank indicator IT.NET.USER.ZS, sourced from the ITU World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database, is defined as individuals who used the Internet from any location in the last three months, expressed as a share of the national population — exactly the named construct. The ITU DataHub page (Source 1) confirms the same definition for Egypt but its retrieved text contains no numeric series, so the World Bank rendering of the same ITU series was quoted instead.
K3.quality_evidence: T1 publisher (World Bank Open Data) carrying the ITU World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database series, the internationally standard source for this indicator; definition on the ITU DataHub page for Egypt matches the construct ('proportion of individuals who used the Internet from any location in the last three months').
K3.scale_evidence: National population basis, most recent published reference year 2024. Value 75% of individuals. A secondary aggregator (CountryDataHub, T5) reproduces the same World Bank series at 74.6484 for 2024, consistent with the rounded T1 figure, but is not used as the source of record because T5 may not carry a statistic.
K3.rung_argument: The value rests on a T1 database entry for Egypt specifically (the country row 'Egypt, Arab Rep. 2024 75' on the World Bank indicator page for IT.NET.USER.ZS with locations=EG). The construct named by the indicator — share of individuals using the Internet, national population, most recent year — matches the source definition verbatim: individuals who used the Internet from any location in the last three months, as a percentage of population. It is national in scope (not rural, not urban, not subscription-based), it is an individual-level user share (not household access, not mobile subscriptions per 100), and 2024 is the most recent year published for Egypt in this series. No adjustment, interpolation or cross-country inference was needed: the figure is read directly off the Egypt row. Value therefore recorded as 75%, which by the stated cut points (20/40/60/80) falls in the 60-80 band.
K3.negative_finding: Level 5 was not proposed because the published value of 75% is below the 80% cut point; Egypt's own series shows it has not crossed 80 in any year (2023: 74.0, 2024: 74.6-75), and no admissible source in the retrieved pages reports an Egyptian figure at or above 80.
K3.search_trail: 1) ITU DataHub Egypt page for 'Individuals using the Internet' (T1, the primary publisher) — confirmed the construct definition for Egypt but the retrieved page text rendered no data table or numeric value, so it could not supply a quotable figure. 2) World Bank Open Data indicator IT.NET.USER.ZS filtered to Egypt (T1, republishing the ITU series) — contains the Egypt row '2024 75' twice (Selected Countries and All Countries tables); used as source of record. 3) MCIT Egypt Indicators/Internet page (T3) — only international bandwidth figures dated 2020, no individual-user percentage; dead end. 4) MCIT Publications listing (T3) — lists 'ICT Indicators in Brief' and quarterly bulletins that would plausibly carry a national Internet-user penetration figure, but the listing page itself carries no numbers and the PDFs were not retrieved; dead end. 5) CAPMAS microdata data dictionary (HIECS 2012/2013) — a variable dictionary with no Internet-use statistic; irrelevant. 6) CountryDataHub (T5) gives 74.65 for 2024 sourced from the World Bank; noted for corroboration only, not cited as the value, per the rule that T5 may support existence facts but not statistics.

K4.source_title: World Bank, World Development Indicators — Access to electricity, rural (% of rural population) - Nigeria (SDG 7.1.1 Electrification Dataset)
K4.data_quality_flag: Modelled/harmonised global tracking estimate (ESMAP Tracking SDG7 dataset) rather than a direct national survey tabulation; a national household survey (NBS GHS-Panel Wave 5, 2023/24) reports a substantially higher rural household figure.
K4.construct_note: The World Bank indicator EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS is exactly 'Access to electricity, rural (% of rural population)' for Nigeria, matching the named construct (rural, not national). For context, the same page's companion series gives national and urban access, and Nigeria's NBS General Household Survey-Panel Wave 5 (2023/24) is reported to give 40.4% of RURAL HOUSEHOLDS with access against a 53.6% national average — but that is a household-share measure from a different instrument, and in the pages supplied it appears only in a T5 newspaper account (punchng.com), not in the quotable NBS PDF text provided. It is therefore recorded as context, not as the value.
K4.quality_evidence: T1 publisher (World Bank WDI), indicator drawn from the SDG 7.1.1 Electrification Dataset compiled by ESMAP/Tracking SDG7, the standard international series for this construct. The page states: 'SDG 7.1.1 Electrification Dataset, World Bank ( WB ), uri: trackingsdg7.esmap.org/downloads'. Series is disaggregated rural/urban/national, so the rural cut is published as such.
K4.scale_evidence: National-coverage estimate for the whole rural population of Nigeria, most recent year 2024, part of a 1990-2024 series.
K4.rung_argument: The value rests on a T1 international database series whose definition is verbatim the named construct — rural share of the rural population with electricity access — for Nigeria specifically, with the most recent year (2024) and value (23.5) shown in the country table on the fetched page and quotable verbatim. No cross-country substitution or national-for-rural substitution was needed: the rural series itself was retrieved. The one substantive tension is with the NBS GHS-Panel Wave 5 rural household figure (40.4%), which would land in a different band; that figure measures households rather than population, comes from a single panel survey rather than the harmonised SDG 7.1.1 tracking series, and in the supplied evidence is only quotable from a T5 news page, so it does not displace the T1 series. A peer-reviewed T2 source in the supplied pages independently cites the World Bank rural figure of 24.6% for 2020, consistent in magnitude with the 2024 series value and corroborating that the World Bank rural series is the one measuring this construct.
K4.negative_finding: Level 3 (requiring >40%) was not proposed because the T1 rural series value is 23.5%, well below the 40 cut point. The only evidence pointing above 40 is the NBS GHS-Panel household-level 40.4%, which (a) measures household share not population share, and (b) is not quotable at an admissible tier from the pages supplied — the NBS PDF text provided contains only front matter and the table of contents, not the electricity chapter. Adopting it would both change construct and drop tier, so it is recorded as context only.
K4.search_trail: 1) Went first to the World Bank WDI indicator page for EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS filtered to Nigeria (Source 1) — the exact named construct; found Nigeria 2024 = 23.5 in the 'Selected Countries and Economies' table and copied it verbatim. 2) Checked the NBS GHS-Panel Wave 5 2023/24 PDF (Source 2) as the preferred national-statistics alternative; the supplied text ends at the table of contents and contains no electricity access figure, so nothing quotable there. 3) Checked the two DataBank embeds (Sources 3 and 4): Source 3 shows only gross capital formation with all values '..'; Source 4 lists chart series labels for clean cooking and national electricity access with no rural electricity numbers in the text. 4) Reviewed T2/T3 literature (Frontiers, MDPI, PMC Heliyon review, PMC Sci Data) — the Sci Data paper cites the World Bank rural figure of 24.6% for 2020, corroborating the series but older; the others give national figures (55%, ~70% energy poverty) which are not the rural construct. 5) The Punch article (T5) carries the NBS rural household figure of 40.4%; rejected as the recorded value on tier and construct grounds and logged in construct_note. Dead ends: DataBank embeds, NBS PDF body text.

K5.scale_evidence: Value applies to the whole rural population of Egypt; the same 2024 vintage is published for all countries in the SDG 7.1.1 Electrification Dataset.
K5.rung_argument: The value recorded is 100.0% and it is a rural-specific figure, not a national one. Two checks support this: (a) the page quoted is the dedicated rural series page, whose URL and title are EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS / 'Access to electricity, rural (% of rural population)', and whose metadata (Source 3) defines the unit of measure as '% (share) of rural population'; (b) the Egypt row in that page's 'All Countries and Economies' table gives most recent year 2024 and most recent value 100.0. The rural and national series are separately published and Egypt appears at 100.0 in both, which is internally coherent for a country reported as having achieved universal access. K7.source_title: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, UN E-Government Knowledgebase (EGOVKB) — Country Information: Egypt (E-Government Survey 2024)
K7.construct_note: The quoted figure is exactly the UN DESA E-Government Development Index composite score for Egypt from the most recent survey edition (2024). The same country profile page reports the more precise value 0.66994 in the historical series row ("Egypt (Value) 0.66994 ..."), and the Data Center league table lists Egypt at rank 95 with EGDI 2024 of 0.6699 — all three are the same construct and agree.
K7.quality_evidence: Value comes from UN DESA's own E-Government Knowledgebase country profile, the authoritative publisher of the EGDI, not a secondary summary. It is corroborated within the retrieved pages by (a) the UN DESA Data Center 2024 ranking table showing "Egypt HEGDI H3 95 0.6699", and (b) Egypt's MCIT reporting that Egypt advanced from 103rd in 2022 to 95th in 2024. The 2024 edition is the most recent survey; the World Bank Data360 mirror of the same UN DESA series was checked but its page text carries no Egypt-specific value.
K7.scale_evidence: National-level composite index covering the whole country; EGDI is by construction a national measure, so no sub-national or coverage mismatch arises. Sub-component values for Egypt 2024 are Online Service Index 0.70016, Telecommunication Infrastructure Index 0.69456, Human Capital Index 0.61503.
K7.rung_argument: The task is to establish the VALUE and its construct match. (1) The indicator names the UN E-Government Development Index score, 0-1, most recent survey. (2) The retrieved UN DESA EGOVKB country page for Egypt states the 2024 EGDI as 0.6699 (0.66994 in the historical series), rank 95 of 193, rating class H3 within the HEGDI group. (3) 2024 is the most recent edition of the UN E-Government Survey among those listed on the publisher's own reports menu (2024, 2022, 2020, ...), so this is the current figure, not a stale one. (4) The figure is for Egypt specifically, read off Egypt's own country profile and cross-checked against the Egypt row of the 193-economy ranking table.
